commit.message:
feat(sim): judge fixture collisions against the fixture's real mesh

The world-AABB fixture laws (c2)/(d2) stay the broad phase; a tagged
model's closed world mesh now gets the last word on every upright move
its box flagged, and may only acquit. A path down a vise's gap - inside
its one box, nowhere near its steel - posts and generates clean, while
a jaw-corner clip, a rapid into a jaw top, a holder over a jaw and a
tool buried in steel still block the post.

Narrow phase (camcraft_sim::fixture_mesh): each band of the stack is an
upright cylinder swept along the tip's chord - a convex Minkowski sum -
tested against facets by GJK, "clear" only on a proven support-plane gap
over FIXTURE_HIT_TOL (+ the arc chord's deviation); a band clear of
every facet is decided wholly inside/outside by ray-crossing winding +
parity with ambiguity rejection. Object-median AABB BVH, pruned by the
same proof. Open, non-finite, collapsed or oversized meshes refuse by
name (MeshError) and keep the box verdict; posed, C-turned, XZ/YZ-arc
moves and lathe tools keep the box verdict. Where nothing is acquitted
the report is the box laws' own, byte for byte.

Refs #339

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge remote-tracking branch 'upstream/main' (#381 HolderStack) into issue/339-fixture-mesh

#381 landed: the fixture laws read a HolderStack. The mesh law follows:
steel_stack takes the same HolderStack (shank, the holder's own bands,
the housing on holder.top), and mesh_refined wraps the *_held laws in
posting::fixture_problems and generate::workholding_warnings - so a
modelled holder body is judged against the fixture mesh band by band.

Merge upstream/main (70c261ba) into issue/339-fixture-mesh-v2

Brings in #464 (fixture-law gaps: stack_span upright rapids + ramps),
#462 (carry-machine check) and #470 (MCP setup/machine/fixture tools).

Conflict resolutions:
- crates/app/src/posting.rs fixture_findings: main (#181/#470) made the
  walk return Result<FixtureFindings, String> with (name, hit) pairs and
  an unjudged list; #476 wraps both *_held laws in mesh_refined with
  steel_stack(geom, holder, spindle) and a per-setup mesh cache. Kept
  both: the mesh-refined bands and rapids hits feed out.hits, the mesh
  refusals are still logged once per setup, and the walk returns
  Ok(out). fixture_problems is main's (strings from the findings), so
  the gate and the MCP get_fixture_findings tool both see the
  mesh-refined verdict.
- Sim side (no textual conflict): #464 rewrote laws (c2)/(d2) through
  stack_span. mesh_refined calls the laws through its closure, so it
  wraps the new laws unchanged; steel_stack is the same band list as
  stack_span::upper_bands plus the flute. One semantic fix: judge_move
  labelled every rapid hit FixturePart::Rapid, but (d2) now names a
  band above the flute by its part - the mesh now does the same (only
  the flute reads as Rapid). Pinned by sim fixture_mesh
  a_rapid_kept_by_the_mesh_names_its_band_like_law_d2 (fails on the
  old label). Recorded in docs/decisions/339-fixture-mesh.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(sim): pin that the fixture box laws already convict every mesh penetration

Slice 2's gate (#339): a meshed fixture's box is the exact AABB of the
vertices its mesh judges, so every silence of the box laws (strict z
overlap, the strict-dip rapid rule, flush contact with a top or
bottom) spares no more than float dust of the mesh either. Pinned on a
mesh top face, a rotated fixture whose top is an edge, an overhanging
clamp arm, the #424/#425 repros on a closed mesh, and a seeded sweep of
12,000 straight moves (7,045 box-silent, 103 flush) where none
penetrates the mesh.

Refs #339
